Lessons.Title: What Attributes Do You See?
ExplanationParagraphs: Original 2021 Grade3 Unit7 Lesson1, introductory geometry under 3.G.A.1, was compared to owner-device local lesson.html SHA256 84fe058ac93c4b2e01899f7e9d8c1aeb17ca9c22c57f1c683a99eeb4c1bc10f6 and preparation.html SHA256 f22dd23ef528474d55d051807dc60ae85c5c729cf578ef4ce513247602055cae. Two original pupil sections are publicly readable; original Grade3 Shape Cards blackline master, stand-alone student PDF, and the publisher's four warm-up source-image pixels have not been independently inspected/certified. First-party content preserves instructions, verified teacher card relations and open classifications but cannot claim publisher card/image geometry parity.

Warm-up Which One Doesn't Belong: Who's in the Group? (10 minutes): four original visual shapes labelled A,B,C,D. Each could be reasonably selected as an outsider under a different shape attribute (e.g., number of sides, corners, equal sides, shading, orientation). Students choose one and explain WHY with reference to pictures; teacher invites at least one reason for EACH of four, not one single correct letter. Original visual shapes cannot be reconstructed or assigned a guaranteed category from short image descriptions alone.

Activity1 Card Sort: Shapes (35 minutes): teacher PRE-CUTS one set of original Grade3 Shape Cards blackline master for each PAIR. First, partners sort cards into categories of their own choosing and explain what property makes shapes belong together. Properties might be sides, side lengths, number of corners/angles, same length, shading, diagonal/curved/straight sides or right angles. Multiple categories are valid and a shape can belong to multiple different groups depending on the rule; categories are NOT fixed as the same class's sorted answer.

Activity1 has a crucial SECOND distinct source step: each partner takes turns SECRETLY sorting the cards into TWO NEW categories without telling their classmate the rule. Other partner guesses the criterion from attributes of the sorted cards; then students reverse roles. Do not remove secret-categorization component or force sorting only by number of sides.

The source teacher introduces the informal term 'angle in a shape' where two sides meet and 'right angle in a shape' for square-type corners. Formal ray-based angle definition and angular measurement are GRADE4 content and must not be imposed in this Grade3 lesson. The teacher's source expressly notes CARD O has FOUR angles and specifically lists cards B,F,M,S as other shapes with RIGHT ANGLES. This is a source teacher text claim, but the corresponding blackline master was NOT visually inspected; no other letter-specific angle properties should be invented.

Original teacher lesson synthesis gives cards A and S as an illustration of different valid groupings. Public teacher model says A has 3 sides and no right angle, S has 5 sides and two right angles, so they can be separated by side count or right-angle presence. Another grouping could use a shared attribute such as equal-length sides, consistent corner-size or both unshaded; teacher explains why one shape might belong in both groups depending on property. Because publisher card pixels are unverified, first-party examples are teacher-guided and not a claim of exact art reproduction.

MLR2 Collect and Display vocabulary: sides, corners, angles, right angles, equal lengths, straight, curved, slanted, shading, triangle, square, rectangle, pentagon, hexagon. Teacher prompts clearer descriptions with drawings and a ruler if visual side lengths are ambiguous. Source restricted Cool-down Tell Me About It is not accessed, no source answer from teacher-gated document claimed.

Source-independent student PDF, publisher Shape Cards blackline, source-art pixel geometry, .NET tests, academic review and Stage D remain NOT VERIFIED. This is an A-B-C first-party semantic teaching candidate and teacher assessment rubric, not a full publisher visual assessment copy.

KeyConcepts.Title: Shape attribute
KeyConcepts.Definition: A geometric property used to group shapes, e.g. number of sides or type of corner.
KeyConcepts.Example: A group can contain all four-sided polygons.

KeyConcepts.Title: Different valid sorts
KeyConcepts.Definition: A shape can be classified in different ways depending on the criterion.
KeyConcepts.Rule: No one mandatory sort when task asks students to create their own categories.
KeyConcepts.Example: An unshaded rectangle may fit 'unshaded' and 'four-sided'.

KeyConcepts.Title: Angle in a shape
KeyConcepts.Definition: In Grade3, an informal corner where two shape sides meet.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Count shape corners/angles; a right angle is a square-type corner.
KeyConcepts.Example: Source card O is described as having four angles.

KeyConcepts.Title: Secret two-way sort
KeyConcepts.Definition: One partner silently groups shape cards into two new categories; the other infers the attribute.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Take turns as sorter and guesser.
KeyConcepts.Example: Guess whether a secret sort distinguishes cards with right angles.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original Which One Doesn't Belong
WorkedExamples.Question: Can A,B,C or D each be chosen as the odd one out?
WorkedExamples.Method: Select based on a justified observed property.
Steps: Name a property differing for the selected shape.
Support with sides/corners/lengths/shading; discuss another defensible classification.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Many valid choices with sound justification
WorkedExamples.Check: Requires access to actual figures; no fixed letter keyed.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original card O corner vocabulary
WorkedExamples.Question: How many angles does card O have, per 2021 teacher text?
WorkedExamples.Method: Informally count corners where shape edges meet.
Steps: Trace sides of card O as shown by teacher.
Describe square-type right corners where applicable without formal ray definition.
WorkedExamples.Check: Source teacher text explicit; card figure itself not source-pixel certified.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original source cards with right angles
WorkedExamples.Question: What lettered cards does teacher name as other examples of right angles?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use verified teacher narrative, not guessed images.
Steps: Teacher checks actual shape cards if using publisher materials.
WorkedExamples.Check: Do not invent properties of additional original letters.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original A versus S in synthesis
WorkedExamples.Question: Could A and S belong together or separately?
Steps: A has3 sides and no right angle according to source teacher.
S has5 sides and two right angles according to source teacher.
Different side count/right angles separates; an actual shared attribute could group.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Either, depending on stated true attribute
WorkedExamples.Check: Teacher checks exact card drawings and logic.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Automatically score one designated letter in warm-up as only correct.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Source asks for a valid reason for each of four choices.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Human evaluation of observed geometric property.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Apply formal rays/degree measurement to a Grade3 angle.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The publisher explicitly reserves the formal definition and measuring angles for Grade4.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use informal shape corner and right-angle vocabulary.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Skip the secret two-category partner sort.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It is a separate original pupil step after first sorting.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Include turns sorting secretly and guessing rule.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Declare pixel-exact attributes of source cards without inspecting original blackline art.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Local teacher text is not an image geometry audit.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Keep original source visual verification as a separate gate.

SummaryPoints: Warm-up four source figures A-D, choose outsider with mathematical explanation; multiple valid choices.
Activity1 partners sort teacher-issued Grade3 shape cards into their own categories, then take turns SECRETLY sorting into two NEW groups and guessing the rule.
Teacher Grade3 shape vocabulary: angle as informal corner, right angle as square-type corner; no Grade4 ray-based definition.
Teacher says card O has4 angles; right-angle examples B,F,M,S. Source synthesis A3 sides/no right vs S5 sides/two right.
Original blackline Shape Cards and student PDF not inspected; publisher Cool-down restricted; tests and Stage D unrun.
